record.paper_title: On open problems of F. Qi
record.context_brief: integral analogue of the exponential-sum inequality
record.original_question: Let [a,b] be a real interval and let f be a continuous function on [a,b]. Determine the integral analogue of the finite-sum two-sided inequality beta_n sum x_i^{alpha_n} <= exp(sum x_i) <= mu_n sum x_i^{lambda_n}; that is, formulate and determine best possible constants for a two-sided inequality comparing exp(integral_a^b |f(x)| dx) with an integral involving |f(x)|^p. The source records only a partial answer: for 0 < p <= 1, it proves the best-constant lower bound (e^p/p^p)(b-a)^{p-1} integral_a^b |f(x)|^p dx <= exp(integral_a^b |f(x)| dx).

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2. What is the integral analogue of the double inequality (1.5)?
In the following, we give a partial answer to Problem 1.2.
Let 0 < p ⩽1 be a real number, and let f be a continuous function on [a, b].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background discrete inequality (for context only): there exist sequences of constants β_n, α_n, μ_n, λ_n such that for all nonnegative reals x_1,...,x_n,
   β_n Σ_{i=1}^n x_i^{α_n} ≤ exp(Σ_{i=1}^n x_i) ≤ μ_n Σ_{i=1}^n x_i^{λ_n}.

Problem. Let [a,b] ⊂ ℝ be a real interval and let f : [a,b] → ℝ be continuous. Find an integral analogue of the above two-sided inequality of the following form: determine real exponents p, q > 0 and the best (largest, respectively smallest) possible constants C_1(p,a,b) and C_2(q,a,b) such that
   C_1(p,a,b) · ∫_a^b |f(x)|^p dx ≤ exp( ∫_a^b |f(x)| dx ) ≤ C_2(q,a,b) · ∫_a^b |f(x)|^q dx
holds for every continuous f on [a,b].

Partial known result: For 0 < p ≤ 1,
   (e^p / p^p) (b-a)^{p-1} ∫_a^b |f(x)|^p dx ≤ exp( ∫_a^b |f(x)| dx ),
with constant (e^p/p^p)(b-a)^{p-1} best possible on the left.

The task is to formulate the full two-sided integral analogue with best-possible constants, in particular providing the (currently missing) sharp upper bound and extending the lower bound beyond the range 0 < p ≤ 1.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals an active literature on Qi-type integral inequalities and related sharp constants, but no source clearly establishes the full two-sided integral analogue (with best-possible upper-bound constant) of the stated exponential-sum inequality. The lower bound for 0 < p ≤ 1 appears in the literature; a definitive sharp upper bound matching the discrete inequality could not be confirmed.

status_evidence.title: On a F. Qi integral inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Qi-type integral inequalities and related conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Active research exists on Qi's integral inequalities, but the specific two-sided sharp analogue is not confirmed solved.

status_evidence.title: On an open problem by Feng Qi regarding an integral inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem by F. Qi on integral inequalities studied with partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Qi's open problems on integral inequalities have received only partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Qi type integral inequalities
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to address Qi-type problems without a complete sharp two-sided exponential analogue.
